summary: Mechanisms enabling LLMs to interact with external systems through structured function calls

content.overview: Function calling (also called tool use) enables LLMs to output structured requests to external systems rather than generating vague natural-language instructions. Instead of returning 'you should check the weather API', the LLM outputs a structured call like 'call get_weather(city="London")'. This is the foundational mechanism that enables AI agents to interact with databases, APIs, file systems, and other external tools, transforming LLMs from text generators into systems that drive real-world actions.
keyPoints: Function calling returns STRUCTURED data (JSON schema-based) rather than natural language - this enables reliable programmatic execution
Tool definitions include: (1) Name, (2) Description (critical for LLM selection), (3) Parameter schema (JSON Schema), (4) Return type
CRITICAL: Tool descriptions are prompt engineering - clear, specific descriptions dramatically improve tool selection accuracy
LLM decides WHICH tool to call and WITH WHAT PARAMETERS - you provide the tool catalog, LLM orchestrates usage
Tool execution happens OUTSIDE the LLM - model requests tool call, your code executes it, result feeds back to model
Context window limits apply to tool outputs - large API responses can overflow context, causing failures or hallucinations
Tool calling requires LLM support - most major providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure) support it natively as of 2025

examples.explanation: Clear descriptions and JSON Schema parameters enable LLM to understand when and how to call tools

examples.title: Tool Execution Flow
examples.explanation: Tool calling is a loop: LLM requests → your code executes → result feeds back → LLM continues

warnings: SECURITY CRITICAL: Validate ALL tool parameters before execution - LLMs can be prompt-injected to call tools with malicious parameters
Never trust LLM-generated tool calls blindly - implement parameter validation, rate limiting, and authorization checks
Large tool outputs overflow context windows - implement truncation, summarization, or pagination strategies
Tool execution failures MUST be reported back to LLM - silent failures cause hallucinations and incorrect responses
Avoid giving tools overly broad permissions - principle of least privilege applies (e.g., read-only tools when possible)
Human-in-the-loop is critical for high-stakes actions - auto-executing financial transactions or data deletion is dangerous
bestPractices: Write tool descriptions from the LLM's perspective - 'Use this when user asks about X' is clearer than technical specs
Implement timeouts, retries, and circuit breakers for external API calls to prevent agent hangs
Return structured error messages to LLM when tools fail - enables agent to adapt or retry with different approaches
Group related tools into logical categories - helps LLM navigate large tool catalogs efficiently
Log all tool calls (including parameters) for debugging, auditing, and transparency
Start with minimal tool set - adding more tools increases cost (longer prompts) and reduces selection accuracy
